prompt:
Write 9 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim, in time order. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1170; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: The claimant reported a rear-end collision at a stop and said the other vehicle struck them from behind while they were stopped in traffic. Initial intake recorded neck and back strain as the injuries described.

Entry 2: The claimant's account of the crash has stayed the same in every conversation so far, including the sequence of events and the position of both vehicles. The driver is named on the policy, and coverage was in force at the time of loss.

Entry 3: Police and two independent witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle and that the impact occurred as described. The other driver has also given a statement that matches the claimant's version.

Entry 4: Photos from the scene show rear-end damage that lines up well with the described impact. Repair estimates for the vehicle follow the same damage pattern, and no earlier damage to the vehicle is known from our records or the prior claims search.

Entry 5: The reported neck and back strain fits the kind and force of a rear impact of this type. Medical records show no earlier injury to the same body areas.

Entry 6: Treatment has continued for somewhat longer than is typical for this injury, with follow-up visits spread over several weeks. The treating provider has documented ongoing symptoms and a plan for physical therapy.

Entry 7: Nothing in the file suggests the vehicle damage occurred before the policy coverage began. The effective date and the loss timeline remain consistent across the policy records and the claim intake.

Entry 8: The claimant is not represented by an attorney and has been cooperative with requests for records and a recorded statement. No contact from outside representation has been received to date.

Entry 9: Based on the current file, the claim is progressing normally, and the bodily injury evaluation will continue once the final treatment records are received. Next steps are to obtain the outstanding imaging reports and schedule a follow-up with the claimant.
